In [[commutative algebra]], '''Grothendieck local duality''' is a [[duality theorem]] for [[cohomology]] of [[module (mathematics)|modules]] over [[local ring]]s, analogous to [[Serre duality]] of [[coherent sheaf|coherent sheaves]].

==Statement==

Suppose that ''R'' is a [[Cohen–Macaulay ring|Cohen–Macaulay]] local ring of dimension ''d'' with maximal ideal ''m'' and residue field ''k''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''R''/''m''. Let ''E''(''k'') be a [[Matlis module]], an [[injective hull]] of ''k'', and let {{overline|Ω}} be the completion of its [[dualizing module]]. Then for any ''R''-module ''M'' there is an isomorphism of modules over the completion of ''R'':

: <math>\operatorname{Ext}_R^i(M,\overline\Omega) \cong \operatorname{Hom}_R(H_m^{d-i}(M),E(k))</math>

where ''H''<sub>''m''</sub> is a [[local cohomology]] group.

There is a generalization to Noetherian local rings that are not Cohen–Macaulay, that replaces the dualizing module with a [[dualizing complex]].
